title: Webb telescope captures new data on star formation in N159
excerpt: Researchers used the James Webb Space Telescope to identify young stellar objects and dim stars within the N159 nebula.
bodyHtml:
The European Space Agency announced on October 22, 2026, that the NASA/ESA James Webb Space Telescope has captured new data on the star-forming region N159. Located 161 000 light-years away in the Large Magellanic Cloud, the nebula is an area of space filled with ionised hydrogen gas where giant molecular clouds collapse to form new stars.

Using data from observing programme 5114, researchers were able to detect stars less than a tenth as massive as the Sun. The analysis distinguished between fully evolved stars and young stellar objects still contained within thick clouds.

The study found that the western region of N159 contains a higher concentration of young stellar objects, indicating it is at an earlier stage of collapse. N159 is one of the youngest star-forming regions of the Large Magellanic Cloud, containing thousands of stars at their earliest stages of formation.
topic: Stars brewing in a nebulous cauldron
